question: Who among the following reformers initially set up a school for girls in Calcutta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was a prominent social reformer and educator in India during the 19th century.
 
• He was instrumental in setting up the first school for girls in Calcutta, aiming to promote women's education and uplift their social status.
 
• Vidyasagar's efforts were part of a broader movement to modernize education and promote gender equality in India.
 
• His contributions also included advocating for widow remarriage and opposing child marriage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was born on 26th September 1820 in Birsingha, Bengal Presidency, British India.
 
• He was a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance, a period of cultural, social, and intellectual awakening in Bengal.
 
• Vidyasagar's contributions to education extended beyond women's education; he also played a significant role in the development of the Bengali language and script.
 
• He authored several textbooks and worked tirelessly to improve the quality of education in India.
 
• His legacy continues to inspire educational and social reforms in contemporary India.
